title: The Depth of Judgment and the Nature of Shame
english: They persecute us; for indeed we become soldiers, approaching them with swords, not in order to strike down, but so that we might suffer nothing.

Regarding: what is the 'confinement'? The 'confinement' signifies many things, but most especially it has become a confinement that is like a gathering of the conclusion, which prevents the impulse of one desiring to philosophize. For even those who engage in dialogue have been accustomed to say, 'I have shut him in.' It also signifies something else, as it lies within the philosophy of Paul: 'God gave them all over to disobedience, so that He might have mercy on all' (Romans 11:32). And observe the sequence of the words: the Gentiles, having believed in the Savior, were descending [into the fold] from the Jews. And previously, again, the Jews prevented the nations from being called unto salvation; for they were saying, 'You are receiving into salvation those from the descendants of your cursed fathers, from idolaters, from many gods.' Therefore, He has made a confinement; He has reproved both.

And such an image is to be used: let someone have a son remaining with him and another cast out because of a malice that preceded. If, the cast-out having repented, the father wishes to receive him in, the son who remains opposes him, saying, 'Does this man become a co-heir with me? He has done such and such.' He reproves even that one upon other sins, saying, 'It is not for this reason that this one is cut off from the lot; and you cast him out, because you have done such and such.' And eventually he no longer argues; for this one too was shut in, that is, he was shut in by the reproofs, just as that one was.

'So that He might have mercy on all'—this is what He has done; for not so that He might prove them to be such, having pursued the reproofs, but so that He might prevent each one from the rest. For neither does the Greek still ascend above the Jews through the cross presented to the Savior by them, nor do they [ascend] above these; for all were found under sin. This is therefore what he says: 'Just as once you disbelieved in God,' you Greeks—even if now you have embraced the gospel and set before yourselves to be God-fearing, but once you also were impious—'but now you have been set free by their disobedience'—if Israel had not been disobedient, you would not have had salvation, for they were arguing and preventing—'so,' he says, 'these also,' the Jews, 'disbelieved in your mercy, so that they also might be set free.' Therefore, as a conclusion, it followed...

For God gave them up to all unrighteousness, that He might have mercy on all (Rom 1:24). The depth of the judgment: 'O depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God; how unsearchable are His judgments and untraceable His ways; for who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has become His counselor?' (Rom 11:33)—the one who shut up all into unrighteousness. Regarding wars, 'shutting up' is taken thus: when every way is removed from them to tread upon and to harm severely; for one is shut up in this way.

Just as the Jew reasoned to himself: 'Do not reproach the sin of the Gentiles; for you also have done the same things' (Rom 2:24). Again, the Greeks who were trampling upon the Jews and saying, 'The murderers and such like.' He says: 'When were you unrighteous? You were idolaters.' Having said to my soul, 'I am your salvation.' Say, O God, truly to the soul: 'I am your salvation.' But when do you say, 'I am the salvation'? Either when you save, or when you bring everything to my soul, leading it toward that same salvation?

Those seeking my soul were put to shame and were ensnared. These are the ones doing wrong, these are the ones warring, concerning whom he said: 'Judge those doing wrong to me, war against those warring against me.' 'They were put to shame,' he says, 'and were ensnared.' It is not possible for anger to be in them, but shame because of the things they they do; for in this way they will cease. Indeed, those having known this, that they have come into shame, say: 'We have slept in our shame, and our dishonor has uncovered us.' It is 'having known,' that they have come into shame and that they were exposed by dishonor.

And this shame and dishonor came from sin. Something like this also in Ezekiel, toward someone being insolent and acting impudently, he says: 'Be ashamed and take your dishonor.' As if someone, suppose, were condemned to serve in public works, such as in a mine or in metal, and thinks greatly upon this, we say to him: 'Be ashamed, know that you are in dishonor.' But—was it the shame of Adam? For not every shame is of the same kind. The scripture itself says: 'There is a shame that follows sin, and there is shame of glory and joy.' And behold: many regarding those things in which it is necessary to sink and to hide and...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Wicked as Chaff and the Angel as Tormentor or Corrector
english: They are glorified for appearing shameful. For the apostle says: 'of whom God is the womb and the glory in their shame, those who think on earthly things' (Rom 8:4). In those things in which it is necessary to be ashamed, they are bold; and we see such things by nature even among men. But he who awaits the Savior, the God Word, knowing that they are being transformed toward the more glorious and toward becoming conformed to the body which He Himself possessed, no longer thinks greatly upon shameful works.

'Let those who consider me evil turn back and be ashamed.' The word 'backwards' is used differently in various places of the Scripture. The phrase 'to turn back to the rear' carries a reproach. For instance, the wife of Lot, leaving from that place of destruction, heard: 'do not look to the rear' (Gen 19:26), meaning, do not set your heart upon that which you are leaving behind. Again, in other places it is said: 'my enemies turned back to the rear.' They turned back to their own rear, so that they might no longer pursue the same path as enemies. 'No one, having laid his hand to the plow, and having turned to the rear' (Luke 9:62). It was not said 'of someone,' but simply 'to the rear'; for when the plowman turns, he breaks the furrow. And the breaking of the furrow hinders the work. It is said that someone turns himself to the rear; this is praised, but this is a reproach. If one hastens to flee a path and turns, this turning to the rear is a reproach. But if someone is pressed toward evil and is checked and turns back by words of repentance, this turning which comes from repentance is praised.

For he says: 'since they pursue toward evil and it is their eagerness to harm me, they turned back from this intention.' Thus, they consider me evil in two ways: when they wish to surround me with sin, they consider me evil; when, wishing to attack, they want to bring something evil upon me, again they consider me evil. The two elders who remained, according to Sosannas, both did this: they considered it evil toward her, wishing to lead her into adultery. Having failed in this, they considered another kind of evil, to overthrow her, to stone her. Consider the same regarding Joseph and Egypt: there too, the matter of fornication was considered evil, e—
To which he was determined to destroy him. However, failing in this, he attempted another way of evils, leaving a slander against him, through which his supposed master was driven as a tormentor.

Let them become like chaff before the face of the wind. Let them become worthless. This is also said in the first Psalm: 'Not so the ungodly, not so, but like the chaff which the wind drives from the face of the earth' (Psalm 1:4). Their worthlessness shows not so much of substance as of intention; for 'those who think on earthly things' (Colossians 3:2), having become entirely of the flesh and of the members, are chaff not having a sheaf, nor a stable seat. Thus a wind briefly moves them. And this wind is able to be either tribulation or a deceptive word. For thus some are carried away by 'every wind of doctrine' (Ephesians 4:14) deceptively 'in the gambling' of those professing that cunning teaching of those practicing it.

And an angel of the Lord driving them out. They have an angel of the Lord driving them out. In the preceding Psalm, 'the angel of the Lord encamping around those who fear him rescued them' (Psalm 34:7). Here, however, the angel of the Lord drives them out, being a certain tormentor sent to punish them. But it is possible and praiseworthy to take the angel as 'encamping around those who fear him'; for the one who uses reproof drives out the sinner, persuading him to depart from what he thinks is pleasant.

Let their way be darkness and a slipping place. Their way—not that of God, not that of virtue, not that of the commandments of God, as it is said: 'I have run the way of your commandments' (Psalm 119:30)—but their way, in which they swell themselves, in which they think they run brightly. Let them know what their way is, let them slip; for this fall is shameful. Just as one who departs from running the straight way falls into a great evil, so the one hastening to run toward evil, when having slipped he falls, takes the beginning of repentance.
And an angel of the Lord pursuing them. As I have said, both reproving and striking or punishing them.

Because you have hidden from me for nothing the corruption of their snare. Evil is often called corruption; for it destroys the truth, makes the inner man evil from good, the just man wicked from the righteous, and the God-fearing ungodly from the God-fearing. And because evil is called corruption:
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Corruption, Punishment, and Vain Malice
english: He says, "they corrupt good habits, bad associations." This corruption—for it is not a physical corruption of the members—corrupts the habits. And the corruption of morals is a moral wickedness. "Bad associations" are deceptive associations.

And so that I may use an image of the prostitute introduced in Proverbs, namely false doctrine or licentiousness: the prostitute woman corrupted the good habits of that young man; for she had approached him with some sophistry. "A sacrifice to me is peace, today I pay my vows"—wherever you wish, the word "today"—"because of this, I went to meet you." But she lies. He did not go out in order to pay his vows, but "desiring." "Because you have hidden from me the corruption of their snare for nothing."

Many errors and false thoughts arise for those unable to distinguish homonyms. The name of corruption and of spoiling signifies many things according to the Scripture. "If anyone," he says, "destroys the temple of God, God destroys him." In this very same expression, two meanings of corruption lie: "if anyone destroys the temple of God" through sin, the body, for "your bodies are a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, which you have from God." Therefore, all wickedness is corruption.

And the kind of wickedness is called corruption, the dissolution of virginity. Thus indeed we say to corrupt the virgin, and to corrupt the child having just tasted of the pleasures of Aphrodite. However, even if the genus of wickedness is called corruption, and even if the species, they are subject to a single signified thing: for such a corruption both destroys and ravages both the soul and the body.

It is said in the prophet: "Because of uncleanness you were destroyed by corruption." And uncleanness of soul is wickedness. It has been said indeed in Proverbs concerning some evil that: "it is crushed because of the uncleanness of the soul." And in the Lamentations of Jeremiah it is said: "her uncleanness is toward her feet," instead of: her way is unclean; for she treads upon the forbidden way of death, the evil way. "Because" therefore "of uncleanness you were destroyed by corruption." And uncleanness of soul is wickedness, as has been said, according to the twofold manner of the said corruption, and according to the genus and the species of wickedness, that is, both according to licentiousness and according to other kinds of wickedness. "Because of uncleanness you were destroyed by corrupt...

And it is also possible to take the other meaning of corruption from this: 'if anyone destroys the temple of God, God destroys him' (1 Cor 3:17). God destroys by testing. And just as the name of loss is taken in two ways regarding the soul, we say both that the sinner suffers loss and that the one being punished suffers loss: 'fear him' (Matt 10:28) who 'is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.' Here, loss is a punishment, which is also called corruption. Thus it is possible that 'because of impurity you were destroyed by corruption'; that is, you have fallen under punishment because you loved to be impure, because you hurried to have the impurity of the soul.

This impurity is the opposite of purity, which, coming upon the heart, brings presence and vision; for 'blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God' (Matt 5:8). Concerning this it is said: 'cleanse your hands, you sinners' (Ps 26:6)—and they become clean when they pursue 'the righteous thing righteously'—but also 'purify your hearts,' and right understanding through the contemplations of the truth. Therefore, 'they hid it from me in vain' (Ps 58:10), wanting to corrupt me to bring me down to wickedness, or even to attack and lead me into harm.

But each of these is doing in vain—for 'in vain' here means 'vainly'—that is, that because I did not provide a cause. The one previously set to act unjustly and to suffer evil rather than to do the opposite will say: 'those surrounding me do this in vain, as God becomes my helper' (Ps 58:10), or: 'they do it in vain because I did not provide a cause.' For example, if Susanna had been condemned by the elders through slander, she would have said: 'they decided against me in vain, since I provided no cause.' Joseph would have said this too, as would the disciples of Christ being persecuted, being denied, and being reviled for the sake of the name of Christ; for if any of the Christians is attacked not for any other reason but because he is a Christian, those attacking him attack him in vain; for sometimes some act against Christians, wanting to harm them, and they find a cause from within them. In vain they reviled my soul. For I did not do anything to cause reviling. And it was also said...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
